short: One of the bloodiest battles of the war, a Swedish victory that opened the road to Vienna.
full:
Fought in Bohemia on 6 March 1645, the Battle of Jankau was one of the last major, and most brutal, engagements of the Thirty Years' War. Lennart Torstensson's Swedish veterans faced an Imperial army commanded by Melchior von Hatzfeldt. Torstensson utilized the rugged, wooded terrain to outmaneuver the Imperial forces, leveraging superior mobile artillery.

The battle devolved into chaotic, disjointed fighting in the forests, but Swedish discipline and firepower ultimately prevailed. The Imperial army was virtually destroyed, and Hatzfeldt was captured. With the Habsburg field army eliminated, the Swedes were able to march on Vienna, increasing the diplomatic pressure that ultimately led to the Peace of Westphalia.
